newsitem.title: UK: Stan Chart extends loss on Cazenove comment.
newsitem.headline: Stan Chart extends loss on Cazenove comment.

text.p: Shares in Standard Chartered Plc on Wednesday extended yesterday's declines sparked by cautious comment from the company's broker Cazenove, traders and analysts said.
The stock was down 12p at 681-1/2 by 0837 GMT, after on Tuesday dropping 17p.

Market talk on Tuesday suggested Cazenove had warned over slowing growth at Standard, but analysts today pointed out it was already known that growth in the Anglo-Asian banking group would slow in the coming year.
"Everyone should know growth is slowing, unless they have been on the planet Zog for the past few months," said David Poutney, analyst at Panmure Gordon.
Yet growth was likely to remain relatively strong, even after allowing for an expected slowdown from the rapid expansion of two years ago, analysts said.
Poutney said that he expected growth of 21 percent next year, down from 27 percent in 1996 and 44 percent in 1993 and 1994. "We are still talking about very good growth," he said.
Standard Chartered spokesman Tim Halford said the company had no comment on what any analyst may be saying or on any suggestion that growth may be slowing.
He said the company planned no further statement on its trading performance until full-year figures on February 26th.
Halford said the company had a "rolling programme" of briefings for analysts and fund managers and was not involved in any briefings above and beyond its normal schedule.
Other analysts agreed that the Cazenove comments appeared to contain nothing dramatically new, pointing out that its profit forecasts had been at the top of the range.
"At the interims they guided people not to get too enthusiastic about growth rates," said John Leonard, analyst at Salomon Brothers.
"To my knowledge there is no new flavour here and particularly on the Hong Kong side there should continue to be a good growth rates."
Said Nick Collier at Morgan Stanley: "There is nothing to change our view, we saw the company recently and we are quite satisfied."
